question: In 2006 a Reuters photographer added extra smoke to a real picture of Beirut after an air strike. What did it cost him?
answer: His whole archive. The strike and the smoke were real; he had used a cloning tool to thicken and darken the plumes, and bloggers spotted the repeated patterns within hours. Reuters dropped him and withdrew all 920 of his photographs, true ones included. Making a true scene more dramatic is still faking it.
move: Exaggerating something true costs you trust in everything else you said.
ask: When I tell a true story, do I ever darken the smoke a little to make it land?
reference: Reuters, statement withdrawing the photographs of Adnan Hajj, 7 August 2006
